title: Moore's trust in his memory; leaving school after third grade
summary: He insists he tells the truth, then explains he left school after third grade and loved the sound and rhythm of drums.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I was so young, a person my age... I think I've done not badly on the (?). I think I've done very good to think. In the teens, up until 83, things have passed, and I think back..
Whatever I say is true. I don't make up. I don't pretend. Hear what I say or you say... I say it, that's the way it is.

Oh, no. Well, there's no doubt that you've had a great and productive life. The Oral History Project is interested in this, because there are a number of things that are important to our understanding of the history of entertainment and Jazz, and how it developed in this country.
Now, you were... When you left home, then had you finished school? Had you stopped going to school? Or did
you leave school also and decide that you didn't want to go back?
I left school. I decided I didn't want to go back. I went to the place for Second and Third Grade. I made the Third Grade; that was it.
I see. And even in school, you were interested in the drums? Was it the sound of the drums or the loudness of the rapping of it, using the chair rungs...?
It was the sound. The sound and the rhythm.

Sound and the rhythm. When I'd be hittin' on it, it would sound like Chinese, because I'd be hittin' on the tin-pan... [DA-RUNG, DONG, DUNG]... Frying pan, on the chairs... Anything I could get a sound, that was rhythm.
I see. But at that time, you didn't know anything about how to use your wrist, rolls and that sort of thing.
